transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've been getting out of breath going up the stairs. It's been bothering me enough that I thought I should get it looked at.
When did you first start feeling out of breath going up the stairs?
Just since last week, I think.
Have you ever had an allergic reaction or a bad reaction to any medicine?
No, I've never had a bad reaction to any medicine.
On a scale from 0 to 10, how bad is it when you get out of breath going up the stairs?
I'm not sure about a number, but I have to stop halfway up the stairs to catch my breath — I never used to have to do that.
Could you tell me what medicines you take regularly, including any that were started or changed recently, and the dose if you know it?

I take rivaroxaban 15 milligrams once a day with my evening meal, bisoprolol 5 milligrams once a day, atorvastatin 40 milligrams at night, and ramipril 2.5 milligrams once a day. Nothing's been started or changed recently that I know of.
Have you ever had any operations?
No, I've never had any operations.
When you have to stop halfway up the stairs to catch your breath, do you notice anything else happening at the same time?
No, no chest pain, and I don't cough up any blood or have a fever. It's just the breathlessness — I stop and it settles after a couple of minutes' rest.
When you get out of breath going up the stairs, where do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
I don't get any pain with it — it's just that I can't get my breath. It's all in my chest, and it doesn't spread anywhere.
Besides not having had any operations, is there anything else about your health in the past you’d like to add?
Well, I've had atrial fibrillation for about 5 years now, and I had a heart attack about 12 years ago. I also had a heart scan at the hospital last year, but I can't remember what the result was.
Is there anything else you'd like to add about the medicines you take?
No, that's everything I take. Nothing else.
Is there anything else about your past health you’d like to add?
No, that's all I can think of.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
